raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Use CUDA-reported free memory for NVIDIA devices reported as integrated (UMA) under WSL, instead of replacing it with WSL guest RAM availability. This fixes startup failures on RTX Spark systems with a GPU memory carveout.

## Claims

- Keep CUDA's free-memory value on CUDA + WSL, so startup profiling uses the GPU allocation budget rather than the WSL guest's available RAM.
- Preserve host-memory accounting for native Linux UMA devices and existing accounting for discrete GPUs and non-CUDA platforms.
- Extend the existing memory-snapshot regression tests and document the automatic WSL behavior in the GPU installation guide.

## Validation

The human submitter reviewed every changed line and tested upstream vLLM containers with and without the patch on an ASUS ProArt P16 RTX Spark laptop, Ubuntu under WSL, 128 GB memory with a 64 GB GPU carveout.

| Model/configuration | Upstream without patch | With patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, FP8 KV cache, 262144 context, utilization 0.8, DFlash2 | Startup fails with “not enough free RAM” | Server starts successfully |

<details>
<summary>Hardware reproduction command supplied by the submitter</summary>

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model": "z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2", "num_speculative_tokens":8}' \
  --load-format safetensors \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

</details>

Local checks:

Post-sync validation on 2026-11-02: merged upstream main `3b6eeb0606` and shortened the documentation note in response to review. The snapshot tests still report **12 passed, 1 deselected**, and pre-commit checks pass. The hardware before/after results above are from the original patch validation.

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py -k memory_snapshot -q` — **12 passed, 1 deselected**. The deselected allocator-profiling test requires a working GPU; this host has no working NVIDIA driver.
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/utils/mem_utils.py tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.md` — passed.
- `.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q vllm/utils/mem_utils.py tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py` — passed.
- `git diff --check main...HEAD` — passed.

<details>
<summary>Before/after regression-test evidence</summary>

The new snapshot tests were copied into an upstream-main worktree at `e811e502efb2b77c7d664b20b68e8dc27e726067`. The baseline test copy uses `create=True` for the `in_wsl` patch target because that import does not exist on main; the baseline implementation was unchanged.

```text
# Run from the upstream-main worktree using the same test environment:
/home/eugr/Projects/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py -k memory_snapshot -q

FAILED test_memory_snapshot_integrated_gpu_accounting[20-cuda-wsl]
AssertionError: assert 21474836480 == 42949672960
FAILED test_memory_snapshot_integrated_gpu_accounting[100-cuda-wsl]
AssertionError: assert 107374182400 == 42949672960
2 failed, 10 passed, 1 deselected

# Run from the fixed branch:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_mem_utils.py -k memory_snapshot -q
12 passed, 1 deselected
```

Initial local setup used `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT=ca5c2d7843a5de396f1a3e4aee137fa16decd720 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto` plus `uv pip install pytest pytest-asyncio pytest-forked tblib -e tests/vllm_test_utils`. At initial validation, upstream main had no published wheel yet; the nearest artifact differed in an unrelated MoE CUDA kernel. These Python-only snapshot tests mock the hardware memory reports and do not execute that kernel. Both revisions used the same environment.

</details>

The utility tests are selected by the existing Buildkite `utils_` step; that CI does not exercise this WSL hardware configuration. The hardware validation above covers the affected server-startup path outside CI.

Model validation is the before/after server-startup comparison above. No accuracy or throughput results are claimed: this change only selects the source of startup memory accounting and does not change model computation.

## Details

`MemorySnapshot.measure()` currently replaces accelerator-reported free memory with `psutil.virtual_memory().available` whenever a GPU is reported as integrated. This is useful on native Linux UMA systems, where reclaimable OS memory is available to the GPU. Under WSL, guest RAM availability does not describe CUDA's allocation budget, particularly with a GPU memory carveout, so the replacement can reject a model that fits the GPU budget.

Reuse the existing cached WSL detection and retain the accelerator-reported value only when the platform is CUDA and runs under WSL. The change adds no options or dependencies and does not add synchronization or transfers to model execution.

Duplicate-work checks found no open upstream PR for `WSL UMA` or `WSL psutil`, and no WSL memory PR by title. Related PRs [#54776](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54776) (ROCm APU pools), [#49760](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49760) (native UMA host reserves), and [#46932](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46932) (CUDA graph estimates) address different behavior and do not contain this CUDA-on-WSL exception. No existing issue is claimed as fixed; this PR addresses the submitter's hardware reproducer.

AI assistance (Codex) was used to review and prepare this PR, run local checks, and add the documentation note. The fix and hardware validation were supplied and reviewed by the human submitter.

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.
